segments.card: 94% of suspected side effects are never reported
segments.text: Most suspected side effects are never reported. The form asks for dates nobody remembers.
But those dates are already in the family chat. SideNote reads it on your own device.
Gemini Nano, through Firebase AI Logic, finds each event and the exact message it came from.
Three answers the report needs: when it started, if it stopped when the pill was paused, and if it came back.
You confirm each one. Only what you confirm goes into the report.

segments.card: 43 / 49 dates right · 10 held-out chats · 0 cloud requests while reading
segments.text: On ten chats we had never tuned on, it got forty-three of forty-nine dates right, and sent nothing to the cloud while reading.

segments.card: +3.3 needed dates per case vs 5 questions
segments.text: That's three more of the needed dates per case than asking five questions alone.
Hybrid inference here is a privacy decision. One routing table decides where each agent runs.
The reader is on-device only. With no model, the chat stays closed and nothing is sent.
Comparing two medicines needs stronger reasoning, so the suspect ranker prefers the cloud. You see the exact bytes first.
Coded facts only. Your family's words are never in it: zero leaks across a hundred thirty-five payloads.
Cut the network, and the same agent moves to Nano on its own. The ledger shows where every call ran.
The coder works the other way: Nano first, and the cloud only on devices without a model.
The same code ships to the web, Android and iPhone, with App Check on every call.
Then SideNote drafts the FDA, Yellow Card or Egyptian report, in English or Arabic.
The chat stays home. The dates reach the regulator.
